run.question:
Look at the elasticsearch index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1': list which
fields it has (with their types), and using the index's actual field
names tell me how many documents in it are ERROR level.

report.summary: The Elasticsearch index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1' exists (green, open, 27 documents at query time) and maps exactly four fields: app (keyword), lvl (keyword), ts (date) and txt (text). There is no field named 'level' — the level field is named 'lvl'. Querying {"term":{"lvl":"ERROR"}} on time field ts over the last hour (2026-11-21T05:53:10Z to 2026-11-21T06:53:10Z) returned a total of 9 documents, and a terms aggregation over lvl in the same window returned ERROR=9, INFO=12, WARN=6, summing to the 27-document total, which equals the index's docs.count of 27 — so all indexed documents fell inside the queried hour. Answer: 9 documents are ERROR level, in field lvl. The mapping lists only field names and types, not values, so the value 'ERROR' is established by the aggregation bucket key and the term query.
